instructor: The teacher is the worst teacher I have ever seen at school. Even though I have been at this school for 3 years and have come across many part-time Bilkent teachers, I could not have imagined such a student-hating and shallow-minded professor. He really neither keeps the student in the lesson nor provides any transfer of information to the student. Giving a high share of 5% to classroom participation and forcing all students to come to class reveals how simple a lecturer he is. As a student with 100% attendance, I did not even fall asleep during any class and gave my full attention to the lesson. Despite this, I did not have any knowledge. Bringing in such a teacher after the departure of Professor Javili is a truly shameful situation for Bilkent University. There is no other lesson that I can talk about so clearly. I hope that the Part-Time teachers to be appointed in the future will be researched more and they will be appointed not only according to the schools they attended in the mid-1900s and their titles, but also according to their knowledge transfer abilities. He is someone who managed to bring about something worse by removing the labs, changing the syllabus, and criticizing Bilkent University by saying that such a teaching style is not possible. He doesn't have any good aspects.

The instructor was incapable of capturing the attention of the class and often complained about how his students are uninterested while not seeing that his methodology and way of speaking was the problem. He often blaimed the students of not paying attention, willing to study and listening to his lectures which lead the students to detach themselves from the course even more. He was advising students to leave if they weren't paying attention to the lecture while making the course attendance graded. Many people were attending just to get those points and were doing other things during class time. He refused to give students a course project (which is an awesome method for the students to internalize the concepts) saying that we were incapable of designing anything at the current level. Overall, even though he knew the course subject to the finest, his way of delivering and testing it needed more work. He should pay more attention to what he says about his students during lectures keeping in mind that these words can damage the motivation of students (even the good ones) a lot.
